ios.desc:
Meet the next generation of your favorite scientific calculator. The official HP 15c app, now brings a completely redesigned interface, a modern look, and improved functionality—while preserving the precision and reliability trusted by professionals for decades.

This RPN calculator offers the features, algorithms and calculation sequences of the original 15c Scientific Calculator conveniently stored on your iPhone or iPad.

The HP 15c You Know – Now Better Than Ever
• Official emulator of legendary calculator device by HP
• Identical algorithms, layout, and keystrokes as the original HP 15c
• RPN (Reverse Polish Notation) for fast and efficient input
• Matrix calculations, Complex functions, Numerical integration.
• Ideal for math and engineering students and professionals
• Programmable – up to 448 lines

Be Ready. Anywhere. Anytime.
Whether you’re in class, at the office, or on the go, HP 15c is ready when you are. Just launch the app on your iPhone and get to work.

Download HP 15c today and experience the perfect blend of classic functionality and modern design.

quotes.text:
I wouldn't say blame in the sense that it implies fault wherein consumers had reasonable expectations to not exist. The 15c was clearly limited production targeting a very niche market (professional scientists and engineers of a certain era). The dubiousness of its release was in the sheer number of them being immediately relisted at super-inflated prices on zero-day.

History tells us that HP made a very clear investment bringing the original 15c to market; it's their IP and their prerogative. I simply can't find reason to fault HP for their business decision, which was likely driven by overall product relevance than cannibalizing sales; 33s and 35s were the only other RPN scientific alternatives at the time, and they're both quite distinct from the 15c. In today's age of touchscreen smart phone proliferation, affordable licensed emulators[1][2] which scale to screen fill that void elegantly...unless you're a modern 20-something-ish Luddite like myself and still don't own a smartphone.

[1] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hp.hp15c15&hl=en

[2] https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/hewlett-packard-15c-scientific/id503720774?mt=8

And oh, BTW, I still have my 15c.

quotes.text:
There’s an official HP version as well:

https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/hp-15c-calculator/id503720774

Yes, their innovation is in hardware, not software.

I also keep my 1986 HP-15C safe and use a DM15L as my everyday calculator (a new meaning for EDC...). In fact I had a NIB HP-15C LE reissue (two, in fact, but one was stolen) and resold it when I got the DM15L (and a second one for redundancy), it's a much better calculator.

I have Free42 for my iPhone and iPad but I tend to use the [official HP HP-15C emulator app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hp-15c-calculator/id503720774) instead, or PCalc.
